title: Playing Bix's horn at Carnegie Hall
summary: Bix's sister asks him to play her brother's stuck old Bach at a concert; he does, and her husband suggests auctioning it.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: For about an hour--
I like to do it about an hour; it isn't really practice - it's blowing some songs---
Warming up---

Warming up. And, uh, at one of the concerts - one of the guys from downstairs - Carnegie Hall came and said, a lady wants to see you and she is with her husband and I said - well, who is it? They said - well, I don't know. They want to see you. So, I said - well, have them come up. We all had our own dressing rooms, at Carnegie. So, here comes a guy and his wife and it was Bix's sister and she had one of Bix's horns - the old Bach with his name on the side. And, she said -- Wild Bill, would you do me a favor - would you play this horn. This horn has never been played since my brother played it.
< The Village Vanguard
And, so, I took it out of the case and fingered it - Christ, it was all stuck and hadn't been played -- I had to have-- I worked about three-quarters of an hour ---
To get it so you could play it--

---to get it so it would play, and, it was a good horn and as I promised her, I opened the first time I was out on the stage and at that point, of course, the Army was--- they were photographing the whole show. There were big klieg lights and flood lights and all this stuff and I played the first set on that horn.
Did you announce that that you were or anything or---
Yes - the announcer did.
That you were playing Bix's horn--
Yeah - on Bix's horn.
So, then, what did you do? Just give it back to her---

I gave it back to her, but there was one thing I could never quite understand and, of course, the sister hit the ceiling. After the show was over, I was upstairs and she came to collect her horn; I left it in the dressing room and, uh, the show-- no, it wasn't the show -- it was at the intermission and he said to his sister, you know---
Who said?
---her husband---
Her husband - okay.

--her husband said to her -- why don't we auction this horn off from the stage. I mean, there's a guy that figured we'd make some money on this old broken down horn and the sister hit the ceiling - oh, she chewedhim out and was she mad.
I wonder what ever happened to that; I suppose she still has it.
I wouldn't be suprised. I'm sure she would never sell that horn. Well, I would have liked to have it myself; it would be anice keepsake - wouldn't it?
Sure it would.
Yeah.
